summary: Extract the package's default handoff — first live slice, else build while the engine reports anything pickable, else hibernate — with a build refusal routing to the inbox slice.
tests: the default handoff names the first live slice ahead of build
the default handoff names build when no slice is live and the engine reports a pickable entry
the default handoff hibernates when no slice is live and nothing is pickable
a build tick the chain declined routes to the inbox slice whatever is pickable
a slice that committed nothing is not named by its own handoff
a declared handoff replaces the package's default
a build tick whose prompt never rendered routes to the inbox slice
acceptance: harness/handoff.ts maps the engine's reported pickable set and no-commit facts onto the next phase, and a consumer's declaration replaces it.
notes: Liveness comes from harness/records.ts and harness/planState.ts; the slice set is a parameter until the factory exists. Reads the engine's reported pickableAfter and no-commit facts only — never a re-parse of an agent stream. Mode names key off NO_COMMIT_MODES as a type, never string literals: .flume/chain.ts:624's ReadonlySet<string> is unchecked. The render-refused leg is new — :929 names clean-exit and not-shipped only, so a walled render re-picks forever. Twins at :686, :920.

tests: the build emits every prompt the package addresses beside dist/harness
pins: the package's files allowlist covers the emitted harness prompts
acceptance: The packaging suite drives the real build and finds every addressed prompt under the emitted dist/harness.
notes: tsc emits no .md, and tests/harnessPackaging.test.ts drives tsc directly rather than `pnpm build`, so the copy step needs one home both can call — that file is the agreement gate's real writer. files: ["dist"] already covers the destination, which is why the allowlist line is a pin.

summary: Ship flume-harness, the bin the package carries beside the engine's flume, and its init verb: the declaration skeleton, the state root, the ignore set and PROTOCOL.md.
tests: flume-harness init writes a declaration.ts skeleton the package's schema parses
flume-harness init writes the state root and its derived ignore lines
flume-harness init writes PROTOCOL.md from the package's own template
flume-harness init refuses a state root that already exists rather than overwriting it
pins: the engine's flume bin exposes no harness verb
acceptance: node bin/flume-harness.js init in an empty repo writes a declaration the package's schema parses, the state root, the ignore set and PROTOCOL.md.
notes: The shim is bin/flume.js's shape — argv through, stdio inherited, exit code out, no options of its own (spec/cli.md, *Distribution*). The files allowlist must cover the template: tsc emits no .md into dist/, and CI asserts the packed set both ways. The skeleton is a TypeScript module (*What a consumer declares*), so it cannot sit under harness/ as a .ts file — tsc would compile it. The engine's verb set stays closed; that is why the verb lives here.

summary: Add the package's chain factory: a complete Chain from one declaration — three plan slices and the fanout build phase, each with its prompt, gates and handoff.
tests: the factory returns the three plan slices and the build phase from a declaration
a plan slice the declaration does not enable is absent from the returned chain
the returned build phase is fanout and carries the declaration's fence
each returned phase names its prompt by an absolute path the package ships
the factory passes the declared supervisor policy to the chain whole
acceptance: harness/chain.ts turns a parsed declaration into a Chain whose phases, prompts, gates and handoff are the package's.
notes: The assembly point: it wires the gates, the judge, the handoff, the entry extension and the prompt addresses, and carries setup, agents and slots through. .flume/chain.ts becomes this factory over .flume/declaration.ts at the cutover — an interactive chore(flume):, never build's (the cutover ruling, 6286ba8).
